exposure: Psychiatric disorders (before, during, or following first pregnancy)
Mode of first delivery (specifically caesarean section)
outcome: Likelihood of a second birth (subsequent births)
cohort: The study included 317,219 primiparous women who delivered their first child in Finland between 2006 and 2016.
finding: Fear of childbirth and psychiatric disorders are associated with a significantly lower likelihood of subsequent births among primiparous women.
mod_finding: Caesarean section as the mode of first delivery decreased the likelihood of a second birth among all women, regardless of fear of childbirth or psychiatric disorders, and particularly for those with these conditions.
followup_time: Up to 15 years (from 2006 to 2021, for women who delivered their first child between 2006-2016)
